prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Select Your Pet Companion Journey", "Choose quick adoption or create a custom pet from your own photos."]
1: ["Preparing Your Desktop Companion", "We are assembling your pet's desktop assets."]
2: ["Sign In to Keep Your Desktop Pet", "Log in with your existing account to ensure your pet data and progress are saved."]
3: ["Setting Up Your Pet", "Your pet will appear on your desktop shortly."]
4: ["Use your primary account to automatically sync and restore saved pets."]
5: ["Upload clear, well-lit photos with centered subjects for best rendering."]
6: ["Generating Desktop Pet Assets"]
7: ["Your Companion is Ready", "Access pet controls anytime from your system tray or taskbar icon."]
8: ["Pet Installed Successfully", "Click the taskbar pet icon to open controls, toggle desktop visibility, or talk to your pet."]
9: ["Meet Your Desktop Companion", "Learn how desktop pets work and choose between pre-made companions or custom creations."]

verdicts.problem: Asks for specific personal account information (primary account)
